 ORDER Heard on I.A. No.9112/2023, an application seeking permission to amend the valuation and accordingly to pay Court fee.

2. Learned counsel for the claimants submits that he has paid deficit Court fee of Rs.8,172/- and in support of the said submission he has filed a copy of Online Court Fee Cyber Receipt along with the application, therefore, the Court fee may be taken on record.
3. On due consideration, I.A. No.9112/2023 is allowed and deficit Court fee is taken on record.

4. This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is filed by the claimants being aggrieved of award dated 26.09.2016 passed by the learned Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hoshangabad (M.P.) in claim case No.400111/2016 ( Smt.Ganeshi Bai and others Vs. Bhagat Singh Yadav and others), wherein on account of death of deceased Jyoti Thakur @ Babli, who was aged about 29 years, Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.2,42,000/- with 8% interest w.e.f. 21.04.2016.
5.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants that deceased Jyoti was aged about 29 years.
Her notional income is construed by the learned Tribunal at Rs.3,000/- per month.
She was daughter-in-law of claimant No.1.
It is submitted that thereafter Tribunal has considered dependency at 1/4 th and then by applying multiplier of 13 has passed the award.
6. Shri T.S. Lamba, learned counsel for the respondent No.3-Insurance Company supports the award.
7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, it is evident from the award that learned Tribunal has not applied itself to the fact situation.

It has neither applied the correct multiplier nor made correct deduction which have been prescribed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Smt. Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009)
6 SCC 121 .

sentences.text:
Since minimum wages even for an unskilled labourer on the date of the accident were to the tune of Rs.6,575/- per month and even a home maker cannot be said to be contributing a lesser effort than an unskilled labourer, therefore, wages are computed at Rs.6,575/- per month or Rs.78,900/-
per annum.
When 50% deduction is made towards living expenses of the deceased, net dependency will come out to Rs.39,450/-/- per annum.

40% is to be added towards the Future Prospects and then, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Smt.Sarla Verma (supra),
multiplier of 17 will be applicable, taking total pecuniary compensation to Rs.9,38,910/-, over and above which claimants will be entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the h e a d of non-pecuniary compensation, taking total compensation to Rs.9,68,910/- against a sum of Rs.2,42,000/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.

9. Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.7,26,910/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs, Twenty Six Thousands, Nine Hundred and Ten only) to which claimants will be entitled to in addition to the amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
This additional amount will also earn interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
10. This additional amount along with accrued interest shall remain invested in the Monthly Income Scheme of the Indian Post Office or a Nationalized Bank for a period of five years.
The claimants will be entitled to utilize its monthly interest for their well being and maintenance, but the principal amount will not allowed to be withdrawn for a period of five years.
11. In above terms, this miscellaneous appeal is disposed of.
12. Record of the Claims Tribunal be sent back.
